title: Finite-power coordinates after scalar restriction detect preservation of finite limits
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small relative to the coefficient universe, with abelian sheafification whose local equivalences are monoidal, and give $\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C,\operatorname{Ab})$ the sheafified tensor product of [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]. Let $\varphi:R\to B$ be a morphism of commutative ring objects [sk-def-sfb-ring-object] of $\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C,\operatorname{Ab})$. Write $\operatorname{Mod}_R$ and $\operatorname{Mod}_B$ for their categories of internal module objects [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], and $\operatorname{Res}_\varphi:\operatorname{Mod}_B\to\operatorname{Mod}_R$ for restriction of scalars [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]. For an integer $n\geq0$, let $P_n:\operatorname{Mod}_R\to\operatorname{Mod}_R$ send $M$ to the product $M^n$ of $n$ copies, with componentwise action, and send $f$ to $f^n$; set $M^0=0$. If a functor $T:\operatorname{Mod}_R\to\operatorname{Mod}_B$ is equipped with a natural isomorphism $\alpha:\operatorname{Res}_\varphi\circ T\xrightarrow{\sim}P_n$, then $T$ preserves finite limits. Explicitly, for every finite category $J$ and diagram $D:J\to\operatorname{Mod}_R$ with limit cone $(L,(p_j)_j)$, the cone $(T(L),(T(p_j))_j)$ is a limit cone in $\operatorname{Mod}_B$, including when $J$ is empty.

source.place: Final sentence: finite direct sums are exact; internal-module limit comparison following the natural tensor-coordinate isomorphism

proof.text: Apply [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence] to both $R$ and $B$. Its hypotheses are exactly the smallness, abelian sheafification and monoidal-local-equivalence assumptions of the item; the tensor is the stipulated sheafified tensor. It identifies each internal module category with sectionwise module sheaves, preserving underlying sheaves and sections. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-limits-sectionwise], finite diagrams in either category therefore have limits whose sections are compatible families, with componentwise scalar action and coordinate projections. This includes the empty diagram: its compatible-family module has one element on every object, so is the zero module, which is terminal. We use these equivalences only to compute limits, not to change the coefficient categories in the assertion.

source.place: Final sentence: the inference from natural finite-power coordinates to finite-limit preservation

proof.text:
Write $V=\operatorname{Res}_\varphi$. By [def-sfb-modobj-restriction], $V$ leaves underlying sheaves and arrows unchanged and replaces an action $\gamma$ by $\gamma(\varphi\otimes-)$. Let $K$ be a finite diagram in $\operatorname{Mod}_B$ with limit cone $(L,(p_j)_j)$, and let $(L',(p'_j)_j)$ be a limit of $VK$ in $\operatorname{Mod}_R$. By step 1 and [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-limits-sectionwise], in both categories the underlying abelian sheaf of a limit is the sheaf of compatible families, with the coordinate projections; so the projections are jointly monic on underlying sheaves, and there is an isomorphism $\theta:L\to L'$ of underlying sheaves with $p'_j\theta=p_j$. It is $R$-linear, where $\gamma_{L'}$ is the $R$-action of $L'$ and $\gamma_{K_j}(\varphi\otimes K_j)$ that of $VK_j$: by $B$-linearity of $p_j$ and $R$-linearity of $p'_j$,
$$p'_j\theta\gamma_L(\varphi\otimes L)=\gamma_{K_j}(\varphi\otimes K_j)(R\otimes p_j)=\gamma_{K_j}(\varphi\otimes K_j)(R\otimes p'_j)(R\otimes\theta)=p'_j\gamma_{L'}(R\otimes\theta)$$
for every $j$, hence $\theta\gamma_L(\varphi\otimes L)=\gamma_{L'}(R\otimes\theta)$; its inverse is then $R$-linear by the computation displayed in step 3 (with $R$ in place of $B$). Thus $\theta$ is an isomorphism of cones in $\operatorname{Mod}_R$ from $V(L,(p_j))$ to a limit cone, so the former is limiting. Thus $V$ preserves finite limits, including the empty one (both vertices are then the zero sheaf).

source.place: Tag 03DB, lemma-limits-colimits, first limit construction; restriction action as in def-sfb-modobj-restriction

proof.text:
The functor $V$ also reflects isomorphisms. If $f:M\to N$ is $B$-linear and $Vf$ is invertible, [def-sfb-modobj-restriction] says that its inverse gives an inverse $g$ to the underlying sheaf map $f$. From the defining linearity equation of [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], $f\gamma_M=\gamma_N(B\otimes f)$, compute
$$g\gamma_N=g\gamma_N(B\otimes f)(B\otimes g)=gf\gamma_M(B\otimes g)=\gamma_M(B\otimes g).$$
Thus $g$ is $B$-linear. Its underlying inverse equations are the inverse equations in the module category, because its morphisms and composition are the underlying ones. So $f$ is invertible in $\operatorname{Mod}_B$.

source.place: Final sentence: the inference from natural finite-power coordinates to finite-limit preservation

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-conservative-left-exact-reflects-finite-limits] with source $\operatorname{Mod}_B$, target $\operatorname{Mod}_R$, and functor $V$. Finite limits in its source exist by step 1; step 2 supplies their preservation and step 3 reflection of isomorphisms. Consequently $V$ reflects finite limits.

We verify the finite-power comparison directly by universal properties. Let $(L,p_j)$ be a limit of $D$ and let $(Q,q_j)$ be a cone over $P_nD$. For each $1\leq k\leq n$, the maps $q_{jk}=\pi_kq_j$ form a cone over $D$, since the arrows of $P_nD$ act coordinatewise. There is a unique $h_k:Q\to L$ with $p_jh_k=q_{jk}$. The product map $h=(h_k)_k:Q\to L^n$ then satisfies $p_j^nh=q_j$, checked after every $\pi_k$; uniqueness follows first from uniqueness for $L$ in each coordinate and then from uniqueness for the product. If $n=0$, every $D(j)^0$ and $L^0$ is terminal, and the unique map $Q\to0$ is the unique lift. If $J$ is empty, each $h_k$ is the unique map to the terminal $L$; the same argument gives the unique map to $L^n$. Thus $P_n$ preserves all the finite limit cones in question.

source.place: Final sentence: the inference from natural finite-power coordinates to finite-limit preservation

proof.text:
Put $F=V\circ T$. The given isomorphism $\alpha:F\xrightarrow{\sim}P_n$ transfers the result of step 5 explicitly. For any cone $q_j:Q\to F(D(j))$, the maps $\alpha_{D(j)}q_j$ are a cone over $P_nD$ by naturality. Step 5 supplies its unique lift $h:Q\to P_nL$. Set $u=\alpha_L^{-1}h$. Naturality gives
$$F(p_j)u=\alpha_{D(j)}^{-1}P_n(p_j)h=q_j.$$
If $u'$ is another lift, $\alpha_Lu'$ has the same composites with every $P_n(p_j)$ as $h$, so equals $h$ by step 5, and $u'=u$. These equations and uniqueness still apply to empty cones. Therefore $V\circ T$ preserves finite limits; this is [lem-sfb-finite-exactness-nat-iso] applied to the natural isomorphism $\alpha^{-1}:P_n\xrightarrow{\sim}V\circ T$.

source.place: Final sentence: the inference from natural finite-power coordinates to finite-limit preservation

proof.text: Finally apply [lem-sfb-finite-limit-preservation-cancellation] with $F=T$ and $V=\operatorname{Res}_\varphi$. Step 6 gives preservation by $V\circ T$, and step 4 gives reflection by $V$. It follows that $T$ preserves finite limits. In particular the cone with vertex $T(L)$ and legs $T(p_j)$ in the question is limiting, for every finite $J$, including $J=\varnothing$.
